classification: Reviewed analytic actual-spectrum normalization under small diagonal dispersion, allowing positive canonical gap; original convergence OPEN
conclusions: For any positive feasible diagonal D with D+-K positive and the separate cap S=tr(D)<=C N^(3/2), write dbar=S/N, delta=S tr(D^-1)/N^2-1, r=(N-1)/dbar^2 and mu_j for absolute moments of the actual full weighted contraction T.
As delta tends to zero, 2Phi(K)/S>=max{kappa(1+r)mu_3/(2r),kappa r/mu_1}-O_C(delta^(1/3)+N^(-1/2)), and mu_2=r+O(delta^(1/3)). Trace optimality and small canonical gap are not required.

The auxiliary principal signing only lower-bounds the original Phi(K). Interlacing loss 2b and congruence moment errors C_j epsilon, C_j=3,9,81/4, return its moments to the full original actual T without replacing its covariance or cross block.
The exact finite phase and nuclear inequalities (4.3) and (5.2) retain their errors. The nuclear denominator is bounded in the correct upper direction before inversion.
Only in the exactly scalar case is mu_3=r(1-gamma) substituted. Its resulting positive-gap phase bound is useful where the earlier masked-gap formula was vacuous.
For an actual final original-zero cell with positive active c=Phi(K), the bound transfers to u_D=c_D/n with extra error at most 2sqrt(delta). General cells retain c/Phi(K).
